payload.title: Chewing Can Help Sculpt Your Face!
payload.summary: Ep. 1,009: Join us as we sit down with Shelly Marshall – also known as Beauty Shamans is an esthetician, former nurse injector, and founder of Beauty Shamans Skincare and the Skin Within Studio. After years of helping people pursue beauty through injections and cosmetic procedures, Shelly began noticing their limitations and that these methods didn't truly solve what people were seeking. Today, Shelly teaches a functional approach to beauty that focuses on restoring facial health, structure, and vitality from the inside out. In this episode, Shelly gets real about facial manipulation, facial exercise, lymphatic drainage, fascia release, and the connection between muscle, bone, and skin as we age. She breaks down how tongue posture, nasal breathing, chewing, posture, and modern habits can impact jawline and facial structure, plus her approach to mouth taping, mewing, myofunctional therapy, and daily facial rituals. Shelly also shares her perspective as a former injector on fillers and injectables, why foundational practices matter, and how to build a more natural, intentional approach to aging well.

payload.title: Neuroscientist: Alzheimer's Starts In Your Nose (Here’s the Fix)
payload.summary: **Visit https://memoryair.com/ and use code DAVE15 for 15% off. ** Dr. Michael Leon on Smell Training, Memory, Sleep, Alzheimer’s Risk, and Brain Longevity Your sense of smell may reveal more about your brain health than you realize, and stimulating it while you sleep may improve memory, sleep quality, and cognitive function. Host Dave Asprey sits down with Dr. Michael Leon, Professor Emeritus of Neurobiology and Behavior at UC Irvine and one of the world’s most cited scientists, to explore why smell may be one of the most overlooked tools for brain health and longevity. Dr. Leon explains why the olfactory system has unusually direct access to the brain’s memory and emotional centers, why smell often declines alongside memory after age 60, and why reduced olfactory function has been associated with Alzheimer’s disease, cognitive decline, depression, and increased all-cause mortality. They also discuss how COVID, chronic congestion, pollution, stress, and aging can impair smell without people realizing it. The conversation dives into olfactory enrichment, including research showing major improvements in memory when older adults were exposed to multiple scents during sleep. Dr. Leon explains why novelty matters, how nighttime scent exposure may increase deep sleep and reduce nightmares, and why olfactory stimulation is being studied in dementia, PTSD, depression, and autism. Dave also explores connections between smell, GLP-1 drugs, exercise, rapamycin, spermidine, oxytocin…

payload.title: Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake
payload.summary: What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. payload.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
payload.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. payload.title: Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake
payload.summary: What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. payload.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
payload.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. payload.title: Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake
payload.summary: What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. payload.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
payload.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. payload.title: Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake
payload.summary: What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. payload.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
payload.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. payload.title: YOUNGER: The Seat of the Soul with Gary Zukav
payload.summary: “The choice that frees or imprisons us is the choice of love or fear. Love liberates. Fear imprisons “. -- Gary Zukav, Spiritual Teacher and New York Times Bestselling Author. Gary Zukav (born October 17, 1942) is an American spiritual teacher, and the author of four consecutive New York Times Best Sellers. Beginning in 1998, he appeared more than 30 times on The Oprah Winfrey Show to discuss transformation in human consciousness which were concepts he presented in his book, The Seat of the Soul. Gary’s first book, The Dancing Wu Li Masters (1979), won a U.S. National Book Award. It is an overview of the New Physics, and became the winner of The American Book Award for Science. Gary’s book The Seat of the Soul, was celebrated as a #1 New York Times Bestseller for three consecutive years in a row. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. She passed on in 2022, and Gary has said, “She (Linda) was a model to me and many others.” Dr. Robyn Benson's next YOUNGER podcast episode is an interview with "The Seat of the Soul" New York Times Bestselling Author, Gary Zukav. Watch, listen and learn from this powerful, timely video…

payload.title: Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake
payload.summary: What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. payload.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
payload.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. payload.summary: “The choice that frees or imprisons us is the choice of love or fear. Love liberates. Fear imprisons “. -- Gary Zukav, Spiritual Teacher and New York Times Bestselling Author. Gary Zukav (born October 17, 1942) is an American spiritual teacher, and the author of four consecutive New York Times Best Sellers. Beginning in 1998, he appeared more than 30 times on The Oprah Winfrey Show to discuss transformation in human consciousness which were concepts he presented in his book, The Seat of the Soul. Gary’s first book, The Dancing Wu Li Masters (1979), won a U.S. National Book Award. It is an overview of the New Physics, and became the winner of The American Book Award for Science. Gary’s book The Seat of the Soul, was celebrated as a #1 New York Times Bestseller for three consecutive years in a row. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. She passed on in 2022, and Gary has said, “She (Linda) was a model to me and many others.” Dr. Robyn Benson's next YOUNGER podcast episode is an interview with "The Seat of the Soul" New York Times Bestselling Author, Gary Zukav. Watch, listen and learn from this powerful, timely video…

payload.title: Neuroscientist: Alzheimer's Starts In Your Nose (Here’s the Fix)
payload.summary: **Visit https://memoryair.com/ and use code DAVE15 for 15% off. ** Dr. Michael Leon on Smell Training, Memory, Sleep, Alzheimer’s Risk, and Brain Longevity Your sense of smell may reveal more about your brain health than you realize, and stimulating it while you sleep may improve memory, sleep quality, and cognitive function. Host Dave Asprey sits down with Dr. Michael Leon, Professor Emeritus of Neurobiology and Behavior at UC Irvine and one of the world’s most cited scientists, to explore why smell may be one of the most overlooked tools for brain health and longevity. Dr. Leon explains why the olfactory system has unusually direct access to the brain’s memory and emotional centers, why smell often declines alongside memory after age 60, and why reduced olfactory function has been associated with Alzheimer’s disease, cognitive decline, depression, and increased all-cause mortality. They also discuss how COVID, chronic congestion, pollution, stress, and aging can impair smell without people realizing it. The conversation dives into olfactory enrichment, including research showing major improvements in memory when older adults were exposed to multiple scents during sleep. Dr. Leon explains why novelty matters, how nighttime scent exposure may increase deep sleep and reduce nightmares, and why olfactory stimulation is being studied in dementia, PTSD, depression, and autism. Dave also explores connections between smell, GLP-1 drugs, exercise, rapamycin, spermidine, oxytocin…

payload.title: Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake
payload.summary: What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. payload.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
payload.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. payload.title: Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake
payload.summary: What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. payload.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
payload.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. Gary’s first book, The Dancing Wu Li Masters (1979), won a U.S. National Book Award. It is an overview of the New Physics, and became the winner of The American Book Award for Science. Gary’s book The Seat of the Soul, was celebrated as a #1 New York Times Bestseller for three consecutive years in a row. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. payload.title: Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake
payload.summary: What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. payload.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
payload.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. payload.summary: Hi HN, I’m Lloyd, one of two founders of RonanRx ( https://ronanrx.com/ ). We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. My doctor suggested tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication. For me, losing weight was only the beginning. "Food noise" was gone. I showed less interest in other compulsive behavior. I stopped scrolling Instagram and quit biting my nails. But that was just the beginning. I was born with a congenital heart defect called aortic stenosis. payload.title: YOUNGER: The Seat of the Soul with Gary Zukav
payload.summary: “The choice that frees or imprisons us is the choice of love or fear. Love liberates. Fear imprisons “. -- Gary Zukav, Spiritual Teacher and New York Times Bestselling Author. Gary Zukav (born October 17, 1942) is an American spiritual teacher, and the author of four consecutive New York Times Best Sellers. Beginning in 1998, he appeared more than 30 times on The Oprah Winfrey Show to discuss transformation in human consciousness which were concepts he presented in his book, The Seat of the Soul. Gary’s first book, The Dancing Wu Li Masters (1979), won a U.S. National Book Award. It is an overview of the New Physics, and became the winner of The American Book Award for Science. Gary’s book The Seat of the Soul, was celebrated as a #1 New York Times Bestseller for three consecutive years in a row. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. payload.title: Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake
payload.summary: What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. payload.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
payload.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. payload.title: YOUNGER: The Seat of the Soul with Gary Zukav
payload.summary: “The choice that frees or imprisons us is the choice of love or fear. Love liberates. Fear imprisons “. -- Gary Zukav, Spiritual Teacher and New York Times Bestselling Author. Gary Zukav (born October 17, 1942) is an American spiritual teacher, and the author of four consecutive New York Times Best Sellers. Beginning in 1998, he appeared more than 30 times on The Oprah Winfrey Show to discuss transformation in human consciousness which were concepts he presented in his book, The Seat of the Soul. Gary’s first book, The Dancing Wu Li Masters (1979), won a U.S. National Book Award. It is an overview of the New Physics, and became the winner of The American Book Award for Science. Gary’s book The Seat of the Soul, was celebrated as a #1 New York Times Bestseller for three consecutive years in a row. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. She passed on in 2022, and Gary has said, “She (Linda) was a model to me and many others.” Dr. Robyn Benson's next YOUNGER podcast episode is an interview with "The Seat of the Soul" New York Times Bestselling Author, Gary Zukav. Watch, listen and learn from this powerful, timely video…

payload.title: 40-Year-Old Looks 20 With THIS Secret Peptide (Better Than Botox)
payload.summary: Carolina Reis de Oliveira on Reversing Skin Age, Menopause, GLP-1 Skin, and the Science of Senescent Cells For Dave’s listeners only, visit oneskin.co/Dave for exclusive early access to the OS-01 Face Rich Cream! Host Dave Asprey sits down with Carolina Reis de Oliveira, PhD, CEO and co-founder of OneSkin. Carolina holds a PhD in stem cell biology and tissue engineering, is a co-inventor of five patents, and has co-authored numerous scientific publications. She and her team are studying skin longevity by targeting one of the central drivers of aging: the accumulation of senescent cells. They break down why skin loses its ability to hold water as you age, and why that process can accelerate dramatically during perimenopause and menopause. Carolina explains the skin's "brick and mortar" barrier system, how declining estrogen affects collagen, ceramides, cholesterol, hyaluronic acid, and elastin, and why simply sealing moisture into your skin with occlusive products does not solve the underlying biology. They also explore why GLP-1 users can experience loose or sagging skin after rapid weight loss and what may help preserve skin structure over time. Carolina reveals how her team screened hundreds of peptides to develop OS-01, a senomorphic peptide designed to reduce the damaging signals produced by senescent "zombie" cells while supporting healthier skin function. In their research, OS-01 reduced markers of cellular senescence and inflammation, increased collagen production…

payload.title: Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake
payload.summary: What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. Turn it down to help people sleep. Turn it up to help people stay awake. Subscribe to Peptide A to Z for straightforward breakdowns of peptide research, clinical studies, and emerging…

payload.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
payload.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. This is a perfect example of why the question isn't simply “Do peptides work?” The better question is: Which peptide, for what purpose, and where is the human evidence? 📘 FREE Peptide Guide: PeptideAtoZ.com/free-guide 💬 Join the Peptide A to Z Community: PeptideAtoZ.com/community 🔬 Peptide A to Z Research. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. payload.title: YOUNGER: The Seat of the Soul with Gary Zukav
payload.summary: “The choice that frees or imprisons us is the choice of love or fear. Love liberates. Fear imprisons “. -- Gary Zukav, Spiritual Teacher and New York Times Bestselling Author. Gary Zukav (born October 17, 1942) is an American spiritual teacher, and the author of four consecutive New York Times Best Sellers. Beginning in 1998, he appeared more than 30 times on The Oprah Winfrey Show to discuss transformation in human consciousness which were concepts he presented in his book, The Seat of the Soul. Gary’s first book, The Dancing Wu Li Masters (1979), won a U.S. National Book Award. It is an overview of the New Physics, and became the winner of The American Book Award for Science. Gary’s book The Seat of the Soul, was celebrated as a #1 New York Times Bestseller for three consecutive years in a row. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. She passed on in 2022, and Gary has said, “She (Linda) was a model to me and many others.” Dr. Robyn Benson's next YOUNGER podcast episode is an interview with "The Seat of the Soul" New York Times Bestselling Author, Gary Zukav. Watch, listen and learn from this powerful, timely video…

payload.title: Do Not Inject Peptides Until You Check This
payload.summary: Peptides are often marketed as if the compound name is the only thing that matters. I think source quality and medical oversight matter just as much. An injectable bypasses many of the body’s normal barriers, so contamination, sterility, labeling, and batch integrity cannot be treated casually. I have only used peptides prescribed through medical doctors, and I would not rely on a polished website or a certificate of analysis alone as proof of quality. Documents can be inaccurate or falsified, and unapproved products may not have the controls people assume they do. My position is not that every peptide is bad. It is that injecting an unverified product is a completely different risk category from taking an ordinary supplement. Curiosity should never outrun basic safety. #Peptides #PeptideSafety #WomensHealth #LongevityMedicine #HealthEducation

The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. payload.title: Gut Doctor: Stop Fibermaxxing! Eat These 3 Foods Instead
payload.summary: Dr. Karan Rajan on Fiber Fermentation, Sodium Myths, and What Your Poop Reveals About Disease Risk Your poop is more predictive than almost any other health signal, and you are flushing that data away every single day without a second look. Host Dave Asprey sits down with Dr. Karan Rajan, a practicing NHS gastrointestinal surgeon, best-selling author, and Chief Science Officer at Throne, who has built a following of over 12 million people by making gut science accessible and actionable. payload.title: Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake
payload.summary: What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. payload.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
payload.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. They break down why fibermaxxing can backfire without the right mix of fast, medium, and slow fermenting fibers, and why generic "eat more fiber" advice ignores what your gut bacteria actually need. The conversation covers protein absorption limits and how much your body can really use, the truth about saturated fat and metabolism, and why the sodium-to-potassium ratio matters more than sodium alone. They also dig into fasting and the gut's natural cleaning cycle, the estrobolome and testobolome and their role in hormone balance and longevity, and how AI is starting to reshape personalized health data, supplements, and functional medicine. payload.title: Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake
payload.summary: What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. payload.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
payload.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. payload.title: How to Heal Your Cells | Dr. Will Cole
payload.summary: We talk about aging like it happens to a whole person at once. It doesn't. It happens organ by organ, at different speeds, and most people never find out which part of them is running ahead until something breaks. Dr. Will Cole has spent sixteen years running one of the first functional medicine telehealth centers in the world, and he came to this conversation with a case that is both clinical and personal. In 2023 his father lost consciousness at the wheel and died in the crash. The autopsy pointed to cardiometabolic changes, and his heart cells had been aging faster than the rest of him. That same year, Stanford researchers found that one in five adults over fifty has at least one organ aging faster than the others, and that when it's the heart, the risk of a cardiac event more than triples. His new book with Dr. Josh Axe, Heal Your Cells, makes an argument that reframes most of what gets called normal aging. Exhaustion, brain fog, the weight that will not move, the hormone shifts nobody can explain. These are not the calendar. They are cells that have stopped reading their own instructions clearly, and that is a state you can change. We get into what actually makes a cell feel unsafe, why your gut lining is one cell thick and therefore the first thing to break, and the point almost nobody makes about elimination diets: the reintroduction matters as much as the elimination, and a protocol you never came off of is a cast you left on until the muscle atrophied. We also get…

payload.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
payload.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. payload.title: How to Heal Your Cells | Dr. Will Cole
payload.summary: We talk about aging like it happens to a whole person at once. It doesn't. It happens organ by organ, at different speeds, and most people never find out which part of them is running ahead until something breaks. Dr. Will Cole has spent sixteen years running one of the first functional medicine telehealth centers in the world, and he came to this conversation with a case that is both clinical and personal. In 2023 his father lost consciousness at the wheel and died in the crash. The autopsy pointed to cardiometabolic changes, and his heart cells had been aging faster than the rest of him. That same year, Stanford researchers found that one in five adults over fifty has at least one organ aging faster than the others, and that when it's the heart, the risk of a cardiac event more than triples. His new book with Dr. Josh Axe, Heal Your Cells, makes an argument that reframes most of what gets called normal aging. Exhaustion, brain fog, the weight that will not move, the hormone shifts nobody can explain. These are not the calendar. They are cells that have stopped reading their own instructions clearly, and that is a state you can change. We get into what actually makes a cell feel unsafe, why your gut lining is one cell thick and therefore the first thing to break, and the point almost nobody makes about elimination diets: the reintroduction matters as much as the elimination, and a protocol you never came off of is a cast you left on until the muscle atrophied. We also get…

payload.title: What Birth Control Actually Does To Your Bone Density
payload.summary: Birth control is one of the most common questions in women's health, and the decision is never one-size-fits-all. payload.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
payload.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. payload.title: What Sauna Research Actually Shows About Longevity
payload.summary: Sauna is one of the longevity practices I use consistently, but the evidence needs to be described honestly. The widely shared reductions in mortality, cardiovascular events, and dementia come largely from observational Finnish data, not randomized trials proving sauna caused those outcomes. The research is still compelling enough to take seriously, especially around cardiovascular conditioning and heat adaptation, but it is not a guarantee. I also track my own toxic-burden results and have seen lower levels during periods when I use sauna. That is useful personal data, not proof that sauna “detoxes” everyone. My approach is to separate established evidence, promising associations, and personal response. Hydration, heat tolerance, medical conditions, and recovery still matter more than chasing the hottest temperature or longest session. #Sauna #Longevity #HeatTherapy #CardiovascularHealth #HealthyAging

payload.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
payload.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. payload.title: What Sauna Research Actually Shows About Longevity
payload.summary: Sauna is one of the longevity practices I use consistently, but the evidence needs to be described honestly. The widely shared reductions in mortality, cardiovascular events, and dementia come largely from observational Finnish data, not randomized trials proving sauna caused those outcomes. The research is still compelling enough to take seriously, especially around cardiovascular conditioning and heat adaptation, but it is not a guarantee. I also track my own toxic-burden results and have seen lower levels during periods when I use sauna. That is useful personal data, not proof that sauna “detoxes” everyone. My approach is to separate established evidence, promising associations, and personal response. Hydration, heat tolerance, medical conditions, and recovery still matter more than chasing the hottest temperature or longest session. #Sauna #Longevity #HeatTherapy #CardiovascularHealth #HealthyAging

payload.title: What Birth Control Actually Does To Your Bone Density
payload.summary: Birth control is one of the most common questions in women's health, and the decision is never one-size-fits-all. Hormonal birth control suppresses natural estrogen and progesterone production, which over time can affect bone density, something rarely explained at the point of prescription. This isn't about telling anyone to stop taking it. It's about making the decision an informed one, including lower-hormone options and how to support bone health if staying on it. #WomensHealth #FemaleLongevity #BirthControl #HormoneHealth #BoneHealth #WomensWellness #LongevityTips

payload.summary: Anxiety in women can sometimes be closely tied to physiology, especially during major hormonal shifts like puberty, perimenopause, and the second half of the menstrual cycle. payload.title: The Mast Cell Connection Behind PMOS, Migraines and Heavy Periods
payload.summary: Mast cells do far more than trigger allergies. They interact with hormones, inflammation, the nervous system, and even blood clotting, which may help explain why conditions like PMOS, migraines, anxiety, and heavy periods can appear together. Dr. Tania Dempsey breaks down why mast cell dysfunction is so often overlooked, especially in women, and why understanding this connection can completely change how we think about seemingly unrelated symptoms.

payload.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
payload.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. In this video, we dig into studies that tested Selank in people with anxiety, including research comparing it with traditional anti-anxiety medications. We also look at the surprising claim that its effects may continue even after treatment stops. payload.title: The Mast Cell Connection Behind PMOS, Migraines and Heavy Periods
payload.summary: Mast cells do far more than trigger allergies. They interact with hormones, inflammation, the nervous system, and even blood clotting, which may help explain why conditions like PMOS, migraines, anxiety, and heavy periods can appear together. Dr. Tania Dempsey breaks down why mast cell dysfunction is so often overlooked, especially in women, and why understanding this connection can completely change how we think about seemingly unrelated symptoms.

payload.title: How Mast Cells Could Be Driving Your PMOS, Endometriosis and Heavy Periods | Dr. Tania Dempsey, MD
payload.summary: Most women who deal with unexplained allergies, stubborn inflammation, heavy periods or a PMOS (formerly PCOS) diagnosis are never told to look at the same underlying cause: an immune cell most doctors were never taught to test for. Dr. Tania Dempsey, MD, trained in internal medicine at Johns Hopkins before leaving conventional practice to focus on mast cell activation syndrome, a condition she believes explains far more chronic illness in women than most doctors realize. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. payload.title: Your Indoor Air May Be Working Against Your Health
payload.summary: Air is one of our largest daily exposures and one of the easiest to ignore because you cannot see most pollutants. I do not think home optimization should begin with buying every gadget. It should begin with measurement. PM2.5, VOCs, humidity, and CO2 can reveal whether cooking, cleaning products, poor ventilation, smoke, or an overcrowded room are changing the air you breathe. Once you know the problem, interventions become more rational: ventilation when outdoor air is clean, source control, appropriate filtration, and regular maintenance. A plant may improve the feel of a room, but it should not replace filtration or ventilation. My approach is to make the environments where I spend the most time as supportive as realistically possible, rather than trying to control every exposure in the world. #IndoorAirQuality #HealthyHome #AirPollution #EnvironmentalHealth #Longevity

payload.title: Your Indoor Air May Be Working Against Your Health
payload.summary: Air is one of our largest daily exposures and one of the easiest to ignore because you cannot see most pollutants. I do not think home optimization should begin with buying every gadget. It should begin with measurement. PM2.5, VOCs, humidity, and CO2 can reveal whether cooking, cleaning products, poor ventilation, smoke, or an overcrowded room are changing the air you breathe. Once you know the problem, interventions become more rational: ventilation when outdoor air is clean, source control, appropriate filtration, and regular maintenance. A plant may improve the feel of a room, but it should not replace filtration or ventilation. My approach is to make the environments where I spend the most time as supportive as realistically possible, rather than trying to control every exposure in the world. #IndoorAirQuality #HealthyHome #AirPollution #EnvironmentalHealth #Longevity

payload.title: Your Indoor Air May Be Working Against Your Health
payload.summary: Air is one of our largest daily exposures and one of the easiest to ignore because you cannot see most pollutants. I do not think home optimization should begin with buying every gadget. It should begin with measurement. PM2.5, VOCs, humidity, and CO2 can reveal whether cooking, cleaning products, poor ventilation, smoke, or an overcrowded room are changing the air you breathe. Once you know the problem, interventions become more rational: ventilation when outdoor air is clean, source control, appropriate filtration, and regular maintenance. A plant may improve the feel of a room, but it should not replace filtration or ventilation. My approach is to make the environments where I spend the most time as supportive as realistically possible, rather than trying to control every exposure in the world. #IndoorAirQuality #HealthyHome #AirPollution #EnvironmentalHealth #Longevity

payload.title: Your Indoor Air May Be Working Against Your Health
payload.summary: Air is one of our largest daily exposures and one of the easiest to ignore because you cannot see most pollutants. I do not think home optimization should begin with buying every gadget. It should begin with measurement. PM2.5, VOCs, humidity, and CO2 can reveal whether cooking, cleaning products, poor ventilation, smoke, or an overcrowded room are changing the air you breathe. Once you know the problem, interventions become more rational: ventilation when outdoor air is clean, source control, appropriate filtration, and regular maintenance. A plant may improve the feel of a room, but it should not replace filtration or ventilation. My approach is to make the environments where I spend the most time as supportive as realistically possible, rather than trying to control every exposure in the world. #IndoorAirQuality #HealthyHome #AirPollution #EnvironmentalHealth #Longevity

payload.title: Selank Peptide: The Anti-Anxiety Peptide?
payload.summary: Is Selank really an anti-anxiety peptide? Selank has become popular for claims involving anxiety, stress, focus, mood, and mental clarity — but unlike many peptides discussed online, Selank actually has human research behind it. In this video, we dig into studies that tested Selank in people with anxiety, including research comparing it with traditional anti-anxiety medications. We also look at the surprising claim that its effects may continue even after treatment stops. So is Selank a legitimate breakthrough for anxiety — or has the peptide world gotten ahead of the science?
